name: apex-flash-1
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (config.json max_position_embeddings 1048576). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: 34 KDA linear-attention layers + 11 MLA/DSA sparse-attention layers (every 4th)
notes:
ADDED 2026-10-25. A rl of zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, not a new base model: same config.json, same 321.323 parameters . Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence mit, repo created 2026-09-30.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT: the only benchmark is the vendor's OWN held-out suite - 60 tasks from 20 vulnerability cases, three views each, adjudicated first-draw pass@1, a single run. It is not a public benchmark and n=60, so the 66.7% vs 60.0% gap is 4 tasks. The card itself says it plans to publish 'more held-out and public benchmark results as they are validated', i.e. this is the first number and nothing corroborates it yet. Recorded because base-column discipline holds (GLM-5.3-Flash is a column in the same table), not because the evidence is strong. 

TASK: pipeline_tag is image-text-to-text and the checkpoint keeps the base's vision architecture, but the card states every reported evaluation is text-only security work and vision 'has not been evaluated'. Recorded as text-generation on that basis; the vision capability is unmeasured, not absent.

benchmarks.name: Held-out vulnerability case eval (pass@1)
benchmarks.config: Vendor's own held-out set: 60 tasks from 20 vulnerability cases, three views each, adjudicated first-draw pass@1, single run. Card table: apex-flash-1 40/60 (66.7%) vs GLM-5.3-Flash 36/60 (60.0%) vs Claude Opus 5 High 43/60. Not a public benchmark; n=60.
